result.topic_en: Derivation of formulas for solving cos(f − ig) = p + iq for the real and imaginary parts f and g, using auxiliary quantities a, A, b, B (referenced to page 287).
result.transcription:
287.a.
Ableitung der Gleichungen
pag. 287
$\cos(f-ig) = p+iq$

$\cos f = c$
$\sin f = s$
$\cos ig = \gamma$
$\sin ig = i\sigma$
$1)\ cc+ss = 1$
$2)\ \gamma\gamma-\sigma\sigma = 1$
$3)\ c\gamma = p$
$4)\ s\sigma = q$

$(1-cc)(\gamma\gamma-1) = qq$
$\gamma\gamma+cc-1-cc\gamma\gamma = qq$
$\gamma\gamma+cc = 1+pp+qq$
$\gamma+c = \sqrt{(1+p)^2+qq}$
$\gamma-c = \sqrt{(1-p)^2+qq}$

$ss+\sigma\sigma = \gamma\gamma-cc = \sqrt{((1+p)^2+qq)((1-p)^2+qq)}$
$ss-\sigma\sigma = 2-cc-\gamma\gamma = \sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}$
$1+p = a\cos A$
$q = a\sin A$
$1-p = b\cos B$
$q = b\sin B$

$ss+\sigma\sigma = \sqrt{ab}$
$ss-\sigma\sigma = ab\cos(A+B)$

$s = \sqrt{ab}\,.\cos\tfrac{1}{2}(A+B)$
$\sigma = \sqrt{ab}\,.\sin\tfrac{1}{2}(A+B)$

$\gamma = \tfrac{1}{2}(a+b)$
$c = \tfrac{1}{2}(a-b)$

methods.what: Setting up the real and imaginary parts of the inverse cosine of a complex number via auxiliary quantities
System of equations for c, s, γ, σ from identities and real/imaginary parts
Elimination giving sum of squares of γ and c
Expressions for γ ± c as moduli
Expression for s²+σ² as product of moduli
Polar-form auxiliary angles for 1±p and q
Final solution formulas for s and σ in terms of a, b, A, B
Final solution formulas for γ = cos ig and c = cos f
